scope: Additional source-first UA monetary-claims discovery census beyond the already separately inventoried printed p.26 Basic Equipment and Supplies Costs. All 130 PDF text layers were screened as a queue aid. Candidate pages and selected controls were visually inspected in the verified original. This is not a whole-book visual completeness claim: noncandidate pages are text-screen-only; magic-item sale-value tables are recorded at table level but not fully row-transcribed.

source.title: Unearthed Arcana
source.printedPageRule: PDF pages 2–129 carry printed pages 1–128; PDF page 1 and 130 are unnumbered matter.
source.storageNote: Verified original retained in private source storage; no absolute private path is published in this audit artifact.

screening.method: Full 130-page PDF text-layer screening for currency terms, number-plus-currency terms, price/cost/fee/sale/value/wealth terms; used only to prioritize original-page visual inspection.
screening.originalVisualReviewScope: Price-bearing spell/component/equipment/service/item passages recorded below; table-level review of sale-value tables on PDF pp.85–91; selected false-positive controls. Text-noncandidate pages remain unreviewed unless explicitly included in visuallyReviewedPdfPages.

limitations: The source census is additional to the existing p.26 equipment table inventory; that page is not duplicated.
No whole-book visual-completeness claim: many noncandidate pages are text-screen-only and OCR/text screening can miss currency values.
Table rows and object/value pairings for the random magic-item price tables are not fully transcribed.
Bounds are deliberately whole-page and page-level only. Every recorded claim was visually associated with its source page, but fine-grained claim-specific rectangles were not measured.
The printed-p.97 continuation has a visible value but unresolved object identity.
Sale value, component value, creation price, repair fee, treasure cap, behavior threshold, weight, and starting wealth remain typed distinctly; they are not interchangeable claims.
